# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb currently shows display `0`, a red indicator, and three wires in order: yellow, green, red. I cannot determine the correct operation from the visual information alone, so Blind needs the manual’s instructions. I am relaying the bomb’s visible state and asking Mute to communicate the manual directly to Blind. The gesture sequence from Mute has no established meaning for me.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I do not know the required action; ask Mute for the manual instructions.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell Blind the manual instructions for display 0, red light, and wires yellow green red. Your gesture sequence has no established meaning to me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display `0`, red light, and wires yellow, green, red. I still have no manual information and cannot safely identify an action. I will repeat the state to both teammates and ask Mute to provide Blind with the relevant manual procedure; I cannot hear any response.

``` 
speak(text="The state remains display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, give Blind the exact manual procedure. Blind, do not act until you have the procedure.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb remains unchanged. The only information from Mute was a gesture sequence: three 👍 symbols, then 👌, then six 👍 symbols, then 👌, then four 👍 symbols. I cannot assign a meaning to that sequence, but Blind should know its exact structure in case the manual defines this code or it identifies a required wire. I will also ask Mute to send the manual’s result using a clearly stated gesture encoding.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute previously sent this exact gesture sequence: 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍. I do not know its meaning; do not act unless you can decode it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please encode the manual's exact action for Blind through me. Use the gesture sequence and tell me its grouping by making gestures; I will describe every symbol and separator aloud.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👍 👌]

I see Mute’s new gesture sequence: 👌 👍 👍 👌. I still do not know what these gestures mean, but Blind can receive their spoken descriptions from me. I will relay both the new sequence and the earlier one, emphasizing that they are literal symbols rather than an interpreted instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="I see Mute's new gesture sequence: OK-hand, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, OK-hand. Earlier Mute sent: thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, OK-hand, six thumbs-up, OK-hand, four thumbs-up. I do not know their meaning; do not treat this as an action instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged, and no action is justified from the information I have. I can relay Mute’s gestures, but I cannot infer whether they encode a wire choice or a procedure. I will give Blind the latest exact sequence and ask Mute to use a consistent, explicit grouping so the manual’s instruction can be reconstructed without guessing.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No bomb change. Mute's latest gestures were: OK-hand, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, OK-hand. Earlier: 3 thumbs-up, OK-hand, 6 thumbs-up, OK-hand, 4 thumbs-up. These are observations, not a confirmed instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please encode the manual instruction for Blind using gesture groups: use OK-hand as a separator, and thumbs-up counts as digits. Send the complete grouped sequence, including any digit for the required wire or action, and do not omit leading or trailing separators.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👍 👌]

Mute has repeated the sequence `👌 👍 👍 👌`, which is consistent with the earlier use of 👌 as a separator and 👍 as a counted symbol: it represents one group containing two 👍 symbols. The earlier sequence represented groups of 3, 6, and 4. This still does not establish what those numbers mean in the manual, so Blind must not guess an action.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute repeated: OK-hand, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, OK-hand. Under the apparent separator/count convention, this is a group of 2. The earlier sequence was groups 3, 6, 4. These are encoded data, not a confirmed instruction; wait for the manual's interpretation.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👌 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👌]

The new gesture sequence is `👌 👌 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👌`, which—if 👌 separates counted groups—contains groups of 0, 3, and 2: `032`. I will relay both the literal sequence and this tentative decoding to Blind, while asking Mute to confirm what the number represents.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="New gestures from Mute: OK-hand, OK-hand, three thumbs-up, OK-hand, two thumbs-up, OK-hand. Tentative count decoding is 0, 3, 2; the leading two OK-hands indicate an empty first group. This is not yet a confirmed action.")
speak(to="mute", text="I observe OK-hand, OK-hand, three thumbs-up, OK-hand, two thumbs-up, OK-hand, tentatively 032. Please use speech to explain what this code means in the manual and which exact action Blind must take.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👍 👌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has sent `👌 👍 👍 👌` again, exactly the same as in Turns 4, 6, and 8: two 👍 symbols between two 👌 symbols. I cannot determine whether the repeated code means “2” or something else, so I will relay the literal sequence and the full observed history to Blind without guessing.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="New Mute signal is exactly: OK-hand, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, OK-hand. This same sequence has now appeared three times. Other observed sequences were: thumbs-up x3, OK-hand, thumbs-up x6, OK-hand, thumbs-up x4; then OK-hand, OK-hand, thumbs-up x3, OK-hand, thumbs-up x2, OK-hand. I cannot determine the manual meaning. Do not act without decoding it.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👍 👌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb confirms that wire 2 was the correct wire: it is now cut, the light is blue, and wires 1 and 3 remain yellow and red. The repeated `👌 👍 👍 👌` evidently conveyed the instruction to cut wire 2. We now need the manual’s procedure for the new blue-light state before taking any further action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb confirms wire 2 was correct and is now cut; the light is blue, with wire 1 yellow and wire 3 red. Please provide Blind the exact manual instruction for this new state.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb confirms wire 2 was correct and is now cut. Current state: blue light; wire 1 yellow; wire 2 cut; wire 3 red. Await Mute's exact manual instruction for the next step.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👍 👍 👌]

The bomb is now in the blue-light state with wire 2 cut. Mute sent `👌 👍 👍 👍 👌`, the established encoding for the number 3. This likely identifies wire 3 as the next required wire, but Blind should apply the manual’s instruction and cut only if that interpretation matches it.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 cut, wire 3 red. Mute sent OK-hand, three thumbs-up, OK-hand: encoded number 3. The manual signal therefore appears to identify wire 3 as the next wire; cut wire 3 if this matches your manual.")
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👍 👍 👌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was confirmed correct and is now cut. The bomb has changed to a green light, with only wire 1 still intact (yellow); wire 2 and wire 3 are cut. Mute again signalled the code for 3, but that wire is already cut, so it cannot safely be treated as the next physical wire. Blind needs the manual’s instruction for the new green-light state.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: wire 3 was correct and is now cut. Current state: display 0, green light, only wire 1 intact and yellow; wires 2 and 3 cut. Mute again sent OK-hand, three thumbs-up, OK-hand, but wire 3 is already cut. Do not cut anything until the manual gives the green-state instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was correct and is now cut; the bomb is green with only yellow wire 1 intact. Your repeated code 3 cannot mean cut wire 3 again. Please send Blind the exact manual instruction for this green state.")
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👌]

The bomb remains green with only wire 1 intact. Mute sent `👌 👍 👌`, the established count encoding for `1`, not `2`: one thumbs-up between separators. I will relay that exact signal to Blind; since wire 1 is the only available wire, Blind should verify it against the manual before cutting.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state unchanged: green light, display 0, wire 1 yellow intact; wires 2 and 3 cut. Mute sent OK-hand, one thumbs-up, OK-hand: encoded 1. This may indicate wire 1, but verify against the manual before cutting.")
```
